entries.title: Colossians 4:3
segments:
.
 

 
 In bonds. the chains with which Paul was bound.

entries.title: Colossians 4:6
segments: Seasoned with salt. So filled with wisdom as to be acceptable to the understanding of those to whom it was addressed.

entries.title: Colossians 4:7
segments: Tychicus. The epistle to the Ephesians was also sent by Tychicus.  See

entries.title: Colossians 4:9
segments: Onesimus. A fugitive slave of Philemon, one  of the Colossian church.  He was sent with Tychicus to Colossae, and bore an epistle to Philemon.  See

entries.title: Colossians 4:10
segments: Aristarchus. A Macedonian who had been a fellow-worker with Paul.  He and Gaius had been seized with Paul at Ephesus, and at the time of the writing of this epistle he was a prisoner with Paul.  See

.
 

 
 Mark. John Mark, the evangelist who was the cause of the separation of Paul and Barnabas.  See

.
 

 
 Receive him. A passing endorsement of Mark, to set aside any prejudice against him because of his former trouble with Paul.

entries.title: Colossians 4:11
segments: Who are the circumcision. The only Jewish workers who were with Paul.

entries.title: Colossians 4:16
segments: The epistle from Laodicea. This letter is believed to be the one now known as the Epistle to the Ephesians.  Many excellent arguments support this view, especially as the oldest copies of the epistle omit the world Ephesus in the greeting.  No other epistle to Laodicea is in existence.

entries.title: Colossians 4:18
segments: Remember my bonds. It was Paul's habit to have his letters written by a secretary, and to write a brief salutation at the close with his own hand to assure their authenticity.  See

.  The bonds to which Paul here refers consisted of a chain joining his right hand to the left hand of a soldier.  Probably it caused such a difference in his handwriting as to require this explanation.
